layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This paper describes a research program aimed at optimizing the composition, heat treatment, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure of ferritic stainless steels for use as condenser tube material in desalination plants. The results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of corrosion tests carried out in a desalination plant are reported and discussed in relation to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: laboratory tests performed on the same alloy compositions. The corrosion measurements are used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outline general methods for maximizing the resistance of ferritic stainless steels to pitting and crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack attack in hot saline environments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The earlier work carried out on this program(1) has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: published previously.1 ,2 It is the purpose of this paper to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discuss the more recent results and to review certain aspects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the earlier work in terms of the potential application of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferritic stainless steel condenser tubes in multi-stage flash

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaporator desalination plants.

layout_dets.text: Summary and Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A study has been made of a series of high purity ferritic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels based on the ternary alloy Fe-Cr-Mo with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objective of assessing the potential application of this class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of material in condenser tubes of multistage flash evapor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ator desalination plants. Laboratory electrochemical tests

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and autoclave tests, which were used for preliminary alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selection, have been directly compared to actual desalina-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion plant exposure of identical alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The following conclusions were reached:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Critical pitting potential measurements, obtained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using a scratch method,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , in synthetic seawater at 90

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C, appear generally reliable in ranking the relative pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of ferritic stainless steels for use in desalination

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plants.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Autoclave tests using synthetic seawater at 121 C

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also give a ranking of crevice attack resistance which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlates well with actual desalination plant exposure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Maximum resistance to crevice attack is obtained by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: raising both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the (Cr + Mo) concentration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. The presence of σ and/or X phase in the microstruc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture of ferritic stainless steels markedly decreases their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance to crevice corrosion in hot seawater. Correct heat

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: treatment of the alloys before use is therefore essential.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. High purity ferritic stainless steels can exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excellent resistance to both pitting and crevice attack in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seawater at 121 C. However, a critical governing factor is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the level of dissolved oxygen in the sea water. In deaerated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seawater at 121 C many ferritic stainless steels have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: excellent corrosion resistance, but with increasing oxygen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content the (Cr + Mo) concentration must be continually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increased to maintain adequate corrosion resistance. Good

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance has been observed with ferritic stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing 21 to 23 wt% Cr and 3 to 5 wt% Mo, when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exposed to 121 C seawater containing 200 to 500 ppb

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dissolved oxygen.
